title: Tyler Teaches: BEGINNER HORNPIPE (Introductory Irish Dance tutorial) 〡Irish Dance tutorial & How To

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The instructor uses an encouraging, friendly, and structured approach, breaking down steps clearly while emphasizing musicality and rhythm. He regularly pauses to explain technique and frame movements with vocal sounds to help students connect sound to action.

lesson_structure.note: Tyler demonstrates the dance sequence from behind.
Tyler introduces himself and the Capezio shape-up class for beginner hornpipes.
Tyler explains that this is a crash course in Irish dance, focusing on 3rd position and rhythm.
Tyler breaks down the first step, counting 5-6-7-8 and explaining bang-step.
Tyler introduces the treble step and demonstrates foot flexibility.

common_mistakes: Dropping the heel instead of staying on the top of the foot
No limp fish (letting the foot go limp during treble)
safety: Don't be discouraged if you can't pick it up the first time around

steps_taught.name: Bang step
steps_taught.description: Full foot in front, tap the top of the foot down on the beat.

steps_taught.name: Treble
steps_taught.description: Elevator ride front foot, brush out and brush back.

what_works: Clear breakdown of sounds with onomatopoeia (bang-step, bum-bum)
what_hinders: Fast initial pace for absolute beginners

quotes.text: One thing I want to definitely get across is that you may not learn it the first time around.
This is all going to be super crash course Irish dance.
Third position is heel to toe with nice turned out inside ankles moving forward.

evidence_segments.observation: Tyler dances a hornpipe routine facing away from the camera on a wooden practice board.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: fast footwork detail and weight shifts

evidence_segments.observation: Close-up of Tyler's feet demonstrating third position heel-to-toe alignment.

extraction.distinctive_method: Uses vocal onomatopoeia sounds like 'bang-step' and 'bum-bum' directly mapped to the rhythm of the steps to reinforce auditory learning.
